reason: Dust falling into the disk plausibly belongs at the young star’s dusty disk, beginning the grain-gathering process.

choice.with: Young star with a dusty disk

expectation: The falling dust will join the disk and become available for grain growth.

alternatives.reason: Slow collisions in the warm disk also seem likely to help form pebbles.

effect: The falling dust has settled into the disk, setting up grain encounters.
reaction: The role of gas drag in concentrating the grains is interesting.
reason: Slowly meeting grains seem most likely to stick to the settled dust and begin building pebbles.
expectation: Gentle encounters will produce larger grain aggregates.

alternatives.reason: The warm disk may instead be the location for grain growth.

effect: Gentle collisions produced fluffy clumps, which may grow further or break apart in harder encounters.
reaction: The contrast between fragile clumps and rocky pebbles is useful.
reason: The fluffy clumps are the clearest starting point for both goals, but their next compatible partners are uncertain.
expectation: Inspection should reveal how the clumps can grow or undergo a hard collision.

alternatives.reason: Fast grains might produce the hard collision, but checking the clumps could reveal other useful paths.

effect: The clumps shattered into smaller grains, completing the hard-collision goal; rocky pebbles remain to be gathered.
reaction: The reversal of the clumps’ growth was a clear contrast with their gentle formation.
reason: Ice-coated grains moving inward are likely to change in the warm inner disk and contribute to rocky pebble formation.
expectation: The warmth will remove the ice coating, leaving rocky material in the inner disk.

alternatives.reason: The fragments might also have a route toward pebble growth.

effect: The inward-moving grains have lost their ice, leaving rocky grains in the warm disk.
reaction: The distinction between evaporating ice and disappearing material is useful.
reason: The rocky grains are the clearest lead toward pebbles, but their next partner is uncertain.
expectation: Inspection should reveal how the rocky grains can gather into pebbles.

alternatives.reason: The two populations of grains might gather together.

effect: Gentle encounters gathered the ice-stripped grains into rocky pebbles, completing the remaining goal; the result also clarified that further sticking alone cannot make planets.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the dry grains become pebbles, with a clear limit on what that growth explains.

mostWorthwhile.text: The hard collision was most worthwhile: seeing fragile clumps break back into smaller grains made the contrast between gentle and fast encounters clear.

leastWorthwhile.text: The final inspection was less engaging as a decision because it revealed only one partner and automatically completed the combination.

surprise.text: I was surprised that inspecting the fluffy clumps immediately triggered their shattering, rather than leaving a choice between growth and collision.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly purposeless, though I needed compatibility feedback to learn how the ice-stripped grains would become pebbles.

continue.text: Yes. I would choose to continue to see what processes beyond grain sticking lead toward rocky worlds; the chapter made that an open question.
